To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the magnetocaloric properties of the composite are better than those of the single magnetic components, (ii) the discontinuous spin orientation transitions are observed for Gd 0. 25 Dy 0. 75 Al 2 and (iii) the composite with Δ S M as constant as possible was obtained
the magnetic entropy changes of GdAl2, DyAl2 and Gd(1 − y)Dyy Al2 (y = 0.25,0.5,0.75) were investigated.
The magnetic properties and the magnetic entropy change of the Gd 1 − y Dy y Al2 (y=0, 0. 25, 0.5, 0.75 and 1) alloys have been investigated by using the Smaily and Chahine model.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the magnetic properties and magnetocaloric effect of the Gd 1-y Dy y Al 1.5 compounds.
the magnetic behavior of Gd 1 − y Dy y Al2 and its possible application as a magnetic material.
the magnetocaloric effects in Gd( 1− y )Dy y Al 2 compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the magnetocaloric behavior of Gd(1 − y) Dy y Al 1.5 is very interesting for applications in refrigeration devices.
the composite with the appropriate concentrations of Gd 1 − y Dy y Al 2 ( y  = 0, 0, 25, 0,5, 0,75 and 1) is an excellent candidate as a magnetic refrigerant material.
the magnetocaloric properties of a composite can be optimized by choosing appropriate concentrations of the constituent magnetic materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the magnetic properties and Δ S T of the Gd(1- y )DyyAl 2 composite can be tuned by varying y.

the composite Gd 0. 25 Dy 0. 75 Al 2 – Gd 0 Al 2 – Dy 0.5Al 2 – DyAl 2 – Gdy 0 Al 0. 2 5 is the most suitable to obtain the maximum entropy change, Δ S T  = 3.8 J K −1 kg −1, for a magnetic field variation of 5 T, in the temperature range of interest.

, in order to achieve a composite with a wide and constant Δ S T in the temperature range between T  = 60 K and 170 K, a suitable concentration of each single magnetic component material is necessary.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the magnetocaloric effects of Gd 1 − y Dy y Al2 are tunable by varying the concentration of Gd and Dy.
the magnetocaloric composite with constant Δ S T in the temperature range 60 K to 150 K can be obtained from the five compounds investigated.
the magnetic field dependence of magnetization in Gd 5 (Si x Ge 1− x ) 4 alloys can be explained by a model based on the competition between exchange interactions and crystalline anisotropy.
